topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives and provides an overview of the canonical hallmarks of cancer within tumor progression models.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how oncogenic mutations in surface receptor pathways, such as Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinase cascades, drive sustained cellular proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cancers in hematopoietic and intestinal tissues disrupt terminal differentiation to trap cells in proliferative progenitor states.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Telomere regulation, senescence bypass, and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the barriers imposed by telomere shortening and senescence-inducing stress signals, and how cancer cells bypass them to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how Krebs cycle mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how developing tumors overcome oxygen diffusion limits by switching on new blood vessel growth to sustain their progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step metastatic cascade, including circulatory routes, biomarker monitoring via circulating tumor cells, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Conclusion and final remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with summarizing thoughts on cancer hallmarks and closing administrative remarks.
